title: RFC005 Stage Gate Policy (§12.2/§14.4, plan spec-stage-gate-report-c5)
$comment: Closed envelope, v1. Carries no embedded self-hash -- like runtime_limits_policy.schema.json, its identity (domain rfc005.stage-gate-policy/v1) is a domain_hash over the whole validated document, computed by the module that loads it, never stored inside it. Exactly 15 contract gates (RFC005 §14.4's fifteen S1/S2 gates); gate names must equal the s1_runner.py GateResult name literals (checked out-of-band by test_stage_gate_report.py against the runner SOURCE, never by importing it). quality and minimum_independent_lineages are closed two-branch unions: the not_applicable branch is the only one this policy's stage (S1/S2) may use (owner R5 2026-09-07, D4) -- stage_gate_report.py refuses to build a document whose quality.status is 'applies' for stage S1/S2, a refusal this schema cannot express on its own since the schema has no way to see the sibling 'stage' field's value from inside quality's own subschema. `stage` names the LOSS POLICY stage this gate policy is bound to (governance 2026-09-07): it must equal the frozen `stage_policy.json`'s own `stage_id`, read and cross-checked by `stage_gate_report.py`, never a free-standing declaration -- a run executed under a different stage (e.g. DEC-009's S2 run evaluated under the frozen S1 loss policy) records that as the report's own `run_stage`, not as a second value of this field. `quality.not_applicable.reason` must say that gate 12's tolerances (atol/rtol) are runner-declared per run and reported in each run's own gate evidence, never a value this frozen policy pins.
